newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso ends firm on stable U.S. long bond.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso ends firm on stable U.S. long bond.

text.p: The Mexican peso moderately extended earlier firmness at the close of trade on Friday as dealers continued to sell long dollar positions, on cue from a stable U.S. bond market, tarders said.
"Local dealers and some foreigners who had gone long stepped in to sell dollars," a trader said.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour stablemate ended 3.3 and 2.4 centavos firmer, respectively, at 7.9680/7.9720 and 7.9640/7.9690 per dollar.
Yields on U.S. 30-year Treasury bonds declined to 6.95 percent, from 6.96 percent in late trade on Thursday.
Dealers said long bond yields had eased slightly following a sharp fall in the U.S. Producer Price Index.
Some traders said the foreign exchange market was stable despite a vote to censure Mexico's anti-drug efforts by the U.S. House of Representatives on Thursday.
"The bill still has to go to the Senate, which won't vote until next week," another trader said, who did not rule out skitters returning to the market next week.

Traders said the peso could lose some ground to the dollar next week with month-end demand for dollars brought forward by forthcoming public holidays, in addition to U.S. inflation data due to be published.
"It is quite possible U.S. markets will come under great pressure next week," a dealer said. "There are predictions the inflation data will not be good."
Mexican markets will be closed for public holidays on March 21, 27 and 28.
Dealers added the market was concerned over the possibility the Federal Open Market Committee would raise U.S. interest rates at its March 25 meeting.
"The market has practically begun to discount a hike in U.S. rates by the FOMC at the end of the month," another dealer said.
"It is possible the peso will trade at more than 8.10 per dollar over the next two weeks," he said.
Same-day peso contracts had earlier closed 2.5 centavos firmer at 7.9560/7.9600 per dollar.
